=== Parentage ===

David Faris's dedicated genealogy of [[Glasgow-12|Robert Glasgow]] and [[Barclay-56|Rosanna Barclay]] identifies '''Robert Barclay Glasgow''' among their ten children. This family reconstruction agrees with the migration and sibling evidence summarized on Robert's profile, so both parent relationships are treated as confident.

== Biography ==
== Research Notes ==
=== Peoria family evidence, 23 October 2026 ===

The published obituary transcription identifies Samuel Steel Glasgow, then in his ninetieth year, as the surviving brother of [[Glasgow-17|Stewart Glasgow]] of Hanna City. The distinctive name and age fit [[Glasgow-9|Samuel Steele Glasgow]], born in September 1814. Stewart’s established Peoria family and independently reviewed 94% paternal identification with [[Glasgow-8|Robert Barclay Glasgow]] support extending the same father to this documented brother. This is a confident combined paternal inference, not a literal statement naming Samuel’s father in the obituary. 92% is a subjective assessment of the complete Samuel-9 to Robert-8 father identification. The obituary supplies the sibling relationship; the 1880 county sketch and 1925 family interview comparisons identify Stewart and support his father. The Peoria Star abstract and Monmouth Review account quoting the Peoria Herald Transcript may derive from one obituary and are not counted as independent parentage witnesses. Published transcription inspected; original newspaper image uninspected. Mother and all vital fields remain separately assessed. The 1902 county-history account of William Steele McCullough identifies his mother as Martha Glasgow, born in Adams County, Ohio, in 1810, and his maternal grandfather as Robert Glasgow. Martha’s husband John, their son’s 26 September 1835 birth, the Adams County origin and later Logan Township family identify the maintained [[Glasgow-11|Martha Steele Glasgow]] account. This combined family identification supports [[Glasgow-8|Robert Barclay Glasgow]] as her father beyond the earlier inherited placement. 94% is a subjective assessment of the complete Martha-11 to Robert-8 father identification. The published transcription names her father and identifies her through husband, son, age and Ohio/Illinois locality sequence. The original printed page has not been inspected; page 749 is a search lead, not a verified page citation. The transcript gives Martha’s death year as 1872, whereas the retained profile says 5 June 1873; retain that field and the discrepancy pending original or vital-record checking. The source does not establish Rosanna’s maternity, Martha’s exact birthday or any older Glasgow ancestry.

[[Glasgow-9|Samuel]] is reassessed 92% and [[Glasgow-11|Martha]] 94%, both confident child placements under [[Glasgow-8|Robert]].

[https://www.werelate.org/wiki/Person:Stewart_Glasgow_(1) Published transcription], inspected 23 October 2026; original uninspected.</ref>

<ref>Historical Encyclopedia of Illinois and History of Peoria County, edited by David McCulloch, volume II (Chicago and Peoria: Munsell Publishing Company, 1902), William Steele McCullough biography; Genealogy Trails transcription, opening paragraph. [https://genealogytrails.com/ill/peoria/bio/biosMc.html Published transcription], inspected 23 October 2026; original uninspected.</ref>

=== Individual father review, 22 October 2026 ===

The existing father [[Glasgow-12]] is assessed at 95% (proved). The held dedicated Faris family account explicitly includes Robert Barclay Glasgow among Robert and Rosanna’s children. His distinctive compound name,1783 Virginia birth and Ohio family context fit that specific descendant household.

Compiled family history95%; underlying Faris pages and pedigree materials were not newly inspected. No genetic pedigree substitutes for parent evidence.

Next useful test: Verify the family-record citations used for this named child.

Source basis already held: [https://search.worldcat.org/title/22731567 David Faris, The Glasgow Family of Adams County, Ohio (1990); specific retained family statements and page citations identified in each reviewed pair]. No new original inspected; no new father attached.
